summary: Orphaned trailing HTML entity and truncated final block after SSE failover behind corporate proxy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long streaming responses delivered over SSE occasionally end with a truncated final markdown/code block and a leftover HTML numeric entity (e.g. '👍') after a network path failover through their corporate proxy. The stream reconnects and resumes but the very last tokens are missing and a trailing entity is left in the last line, causing downstream markdown renderers to break.
impact: Several API calls from BrightBoard production workloads return incomplete final paragraphs or malformed markdown on ~0.5% of streaming sessions during business hours, causing UI errors and automated parsing failures. Customer reports user-visible failures for their summary-generation flow.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use SSE streaming endpoint with conversation length > 800 tokens and markdown output enabled
2) Put client behind a corporate proxy that performs an HTTP 100-Continue handshake and sometimes re-routes connections during idle probes
3) Start stream, simulate a path migration (NAT/idle-probe) from client network or trigger proxy connection splice
4) Observe resumed stream output for missing terminal tokens and presence of a trailing numeric HTML entity in the final line
5) Reproduce more reliably by adding a 1-3s intermittent packet loss during the final chunk window and by enabling aggressive proxy keepalive rebinds

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: proxy path splice is splitting a UTF-8 multi-byte emoji sequence across the final chunk boundary, and our reassembly logic for resume assumes chunk-aligned UTF-8 boundaries; trailing bytes are being interpreted as HTML entities during downstream JSON/markdown framing
Reproduced internally with synthetic proxy rebind using corp-proxy-sim v0.9 and observed identical orphaned numeric entity present only when rebind occurs in the middle of a multi-byte sequence

Observed that SSE resume uses byte-oriented offsets from runtime; however some edge proxies perform transparent header/body rewrites (100-Continue) which incrementally alter chunk boundaries leading to mismatch between resume_offset and actual re-streamed payload

Found related flaky unit in streaming parser: parser/streaming_assembler.go: line 278 does a 'if resumeOffset == savedOffset' fast path that doesn't validate UTF-8 tail bytes; added a failing test case locally

Checked model generation: final tokens include emoji or characters that encode as 4-byte UTF-8 sequences (e.g. thumbs-up). This interacts with chunking where a split can leave 1-3 continuation bytes orphaned

Edge note: customer uses an enterprise WAF that rewrites chunking on TLS termination; WAF adds '100-Continue' handling and sometimes re-chunks responses into smaller segments during spike backpressure

resolution: Workaround provided and engineering patch merged. Short-term: advised customer to configure their WAF to disable chunk rewriting for streaming endpoints or to whitelist our streaming path. Long-term: merged patch (PR 4991) validates UTF-8 tail bytes on resume and falls back to conservative re-synchronization (re-stream from previous safe offset) when mismatch detected. Rollout plan: canary to 10% of hosts 2026-03-06, full rollout 2026-03-09. Postmortem and runbook update scheduled.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add automated e2e test that simulates proxy rebind with mid-multibyte-split and assert final payload integrity
2) Update streaming resume runbook with instructions to detect 'orphaned_utf8_bytes' metric and recommend proxy config
3) Notify customers in enterprise tier with WAF appliances about the configuration change and provide migration guidance
4) Instrumentation: export 'resume_byte_mismatch' metric to console and set alert P1 when > 0.1% of streams in a rolling 1h window
